report.tagline: A US online clinic that sells monthly treatment subscriptions for weight loss, hair loss, sexual health, skin and mental health, with a doctor visit done through an app.
report.simpleSummary: Hims & Hers lets you get treatment for things people feel awkward about, like hair loss, erectile dysfunction or weight, without going to a clinic. You answer questions online, a licensed doctor or nurse reviews them, and if suitable, medicine arrives at your door every month. You pay a monthly subscription that covers the consult and the medicine. Weight-loss drugs pushed revenue to about $890 million in a single quarter in 2026, but that growth also brought fights with regulators and lower margins.

overview.whatItDoes: Hims (for men) and Hers (for women) are two brands of one company that sells telehealth treatment plans. Categories include hair loss, sexual health, weight loss, dermatology, mental health, menopause and, from late 2026, testosterone therapy. A clinician on the platform prescribes, and Hims ships the medicine from its own pharmacies or partners. It now also offers branded weight-loss drugs from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk on the platform, and operates in the UK and Germany after buying Zava.
howItWorks: A customer picks a condition on the website or app and fills in an online medical questionnaire.
A licensed provider reviews it, sometimes with a message or video chat, and prescribes if suitable.
Medicine is made or packed in Hims-owned or partner pharmacies, often as personalised doses or combinations.
The customer pays a monthly or multi-month subscription that includes the consult and medicine.
Refills ship automatically; customers can message providers to adjust treatment.
Lab testing and AI tools are being added to make treatment more personal.
overview.valueProposition: Private, fast and convenient treatment for common and sometimes embarrassing conditions, at a clear monthly price, without insurance or a clinic visit.

businessModel.summary: Hims & Hers sells subscriptions that bundle an online consult with medicine. Customers pay cash, not through insurance. It makes most money on cheap generic or personalised medicines sold at a markup, and less on branded weight-loss drugs.

revenueStreams.detail: Oral, compounded and branded GLP-1 plans. The fastest-growing part, but lower margin.
ED and premature ejaculation treatments, often personalised.
Monthly treatments for hair, acne and anti-ageing.

revenueStreams.stream: Mental health, menopause, testosterone and other
revenueStreams.detail: Newer categories; testosterone and Peptides Plus launched in late 2026.
Online clinics in the UK and Germany.

businessModel.pricing: Prices are shown on the site and change often. Hair loss plans start around $20 to $40 a month, sexual health from a few dollars per dose, and weight-loss plans range from under $100 a month for oral options to several hundred dollars for GLP-1 injections.
costDrivers: Cost of medicine, especially branded GLP-1 drugs
Marketing, including TV and Super Bowl ads
businessModel.unitEconomics: An average subscriber pays about $105 a month (our estimate). In Q3 2026 Hims kept about 57 cents of each dollar after drug and fulfilment costs, so roughly $60 a month per subscriber. That pays for marketing to win new customers, providers and overheads. Branded weight-loss drugs bring high revenue per customer but a smaller share of profit, which is why gross margin dropped from 74% to 57%. The model works when customers stay many months so that CAC (the cost to win each one) is paid back.

howTheyGetUsers: Heavy TV, social media and Super Bowl advertising
New categories that bring in new kinds of customers
whatBringsUsersBack: Ongoing treatment for chronic conditions like hair loss and weight
Cross-selling a second category to existing customers
growth.moat: Hims has a strong consumer brand, its own pharmacies and a large base of 2.8 million subscribers, which makes marketing and production cheaper per customer. But the core service is easy to copy, and drugmakers like Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk sell directly too, so the moat depends on brand and personalisation more than on anything locked in.

improvementIdeas.idea: One-click cancel and a reminder email three days before each charge
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer complaints and legal risk, more trust that brings people back later.

improvementIdeas.idea: Side-effect check-in in week 2 of every new treatment, with fast provider reply
improvementIdeas.problem: Patients quit early because of side effects.

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear comparison page for weight-loss options: branded vs oral vs compounded, with safety and price
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers are confused and worried after FDA warnings.

improvementIdeas.problem: Branded drugs have thin margins and are sold elsewhere too.

pmLessons: Removing shame is a product feature. Hims grew by making awkward care feel normal and private.
Revenue growth can hide weaker unit economics. Watch margin and retention, not only the top line.
In regulated markets, the regulator is a stakeholder. Fast moves can be undone overnight.
Subscriptions build recurring revenue, but hard-to-cancel flows destroy trust and invite lawsuits.

interviewQuestions.question: Revenue grew 49% but subscribers only 13%. What does that tell you?
interviewQuestions.hint: Revenue per subscriber is rising, mostly from pricier weight-loss drugs. Discuss margin, concentration risk and retention.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you decide which new condition Hims should add next?
interviewQuestions.hint: Score by market size, stigma, need for ongoing treatment, regulatory risk and fit with pharmacy capabilities.

interviewQuestions.question: Eli Lilly sells directly. Why would a patient buy Lilly's drug through Hims?
interviewQuestions.hint: Convenience, bundled care, multi-category, brand, coaching. Define what extra value Hims adds and how to measure it.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a better cancellation flow that balances retention and trust.
interviewQuestions.hint: Make cancel easy, offer pause and downgrade, explain renewals, and measure complaints plus win-back rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star metric would you set for Hims & Hers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Retained subscribers on treatment; show drivers (acquisition, retention, cross-sell, outcomes) and guardrails like safety.
